meta.scalability_note: On-premise infrastructure scales only with hardware procurement cycles; no elastic auto-scaling; capacity must be over-provisioned; no global regions or CDN edge; high CapEx for growth
meta.performance_note: Performance depends entirely on hardware investment and team expertise; no vendor SLA; typical enterprise on-premise targets 99.9% uptime; no geo-redundancy without significant additional investment

AWS Amplify.note: No managed web/mobile app hosting platform. Self-hosted on Nginx/Apache or Kubernetes ingress.

AWS Lambda.note: No managed FaaS. Self-hosted alternatives: OpenFaaS, Knative, or Apache OpenWhisk on Kubernetes.

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container orchestration. Self-hosted Docker Swarm or Kubernetes required.

Amazon EKS.note: No managed Kubernetes. Self-managed kubeadm or Rancher cluster on bare metal or VMware.

Amazon EC2.note: Virtual machines available via on-premise hypervisor (VMware vSphere, KVM, Hyper-V). No elastic provisioning; manual sizing and lifecycle management required.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch service. Self-hosted schedulers (Slurm, Apache Airflow) required.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS deployment platform. Manual deployment pipelines required.

Amazon S3.note: No managed object storage. Self-hosted alternatives: MinIO on Kubernetes, Ceph RadosGW. Requires dedicated ops team.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No managed archival storage. Tape libraries or cold-tier NAS solutions required.

Amazon EBS.note: Block storage available via on-premise SAN (NetApp, Pure Storage, Dell EMC). No elastic provisioning; manual LUN management required.

AWS Backup.note: No managed centralised backup. Self-hosted Veeam, Bacula, or Commvault required.

Amazon EFS.note: Shared file system available via on-premise NFS/CIFS servers. No elastic capacity; manual management required.

Amazon RDS.note: No managed database service. Self-hosted PostgreSQL/MySQL on VMs. Manual patching, backup, and failover configuration required.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: No managed document database. Self-hosted MongoDB on VMs.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed NoSQL key-value store. Self-hosted Cassandra or Redis required.

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed time-series database. Self-hosted InfluxDB or TimescaleDB required.

Amazon Aurora.note: No Aurora equivalent on-premise. Self-hosted PostgreSQL/MySQL clusters.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: No managed caching. Self-hosted Redis or Memcached on VMs.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed data warehouse. Self-hosted Greenplum or ClickHouse on bare metal.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: No managed ALB. Self-hosted HAProxy or Nginx Plus required.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: No managed NLB. Physical or virtual load balancers (F5, HAProxy) required.

Amazon VPC.note: Network isolation via VLANs and physical firewalls (Cisco, Palo Alto). No software-defined networking; manual VLAN provisioning by network team.

Amazon Route 53.note: No managed cloud DNS. Self-hosted BIND or Microsoft DNS on-premise.

Amazon API Gateway.note: No managed API gateway. Self-hosted Kong, Traefik, or NGINX required.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No CDN. Third-party CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai) required at additional cost.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Not applicable — on-premise infrastructure already uses direct physical networking.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision API. Self-hosted models (OpenCV, TensorFlow) on GPU servers.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed ML platform. Self-hosted MLflow + Jupyter + GPU servers required.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed GenAI API. Self-hosted LLMs (Ollama, vLLM) on GPU hardware.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL service. Self-hosted Apache Airflow or Spark pipelines.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data cluster. Self-hosted Hadoop/Spark on bare metal.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless SQL analytics. Self-hosted Trino or ClickHouse required.

AWS IAM.note: No managed cloud IAM. On-premise Active Directory or LDAP provides identity; no cloud-native resource policy engine.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed user pool. Self-hosted Keycloak or Auth0 on-premise.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No managed SSO. On-premise ADFS or self-hosted Keycloak required.

AWS KMS.note: No managed KMS. On-premise HSM (Thales, Utimaco) or manual key management required.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: No managed secrets service. Self-hosted HashiCorp Vault required.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: No managed certificate service. Manual TLS certificate procurement and renewal by ops team.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: No managed threat detection. On-premise SIEM (Splunk, IBM QRadar) required.

AWS Security Hub.note: No managed security posture dashboard. Manual compliance tooling required.

AWS Config.note: No managed config compliance. Self-hosted Ansible/Chef compliance scanning required.

AWS Shield.note: No managed DDoS protection. On-premise firewalls (Palo Alto, Fortinet) provide limited DDoS mitigation.

AWS WAF.note: No managed WAF. Self-hosted ModSecurity or commercial WAF appliance required.

AWS CloudTrail.note: No managed audit trail. On-premise syslog/SIEM required for API and system audit logging.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: No managed monitoring. Self-hosted Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager stack required.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed pub/sub. Self-hosted RabbitMQ or NATS for notification routing.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed operations platform. Self-hosted Ansible AWX or Puppet Enterprise required.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: No cloud cost dashboard. CapEx-based accounting via ERP (SAP, Oracle); no real-time resource cost visibility.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI build service. Self-hosted Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions runners required.

AWS CodeDeploy.note: No managed deployment automation. Self-hosted Ansible, Spinnaker, or ArgoCD required.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed pipeline orchestration. Self-hosted GitLab CI/CD or Jenkins pipelines required.

Amazon ECR.note: No managed container registry. Self-hosted Harbor or Docker Registry required.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No managed IaC service. Self-managed Terraform, Ansible, or Pulumi on-premise.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT broker. Self-hosted Eclipse Mosquitto or EMQX MQTT broker required.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed device registry. Self-hosted ThingsBoard or custom device management solution required.

Amazon SQS.note: No managed message queue. Self-hosted RabbitMQ or ActiveMQ required.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus. Self-hosted Kafka or NATS JetStream required.

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed workflow orchestration. Self-hosted Apache Airflow or Temporal required.

Amazon SES.note: No managed email service. Self-hosted Postfix/Sendmail or on-premise Exchange required.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed streaming service. Self-hosted Apache Kafka on bare metal required.
